title: Understanding Gradient Descent
text: Gradient descent is an iterative optimization algorithm used to find the minimum of a function. It updates parameters in the opposite direction of the gradient of the function with respect to the parameters.

title: Convergence of Gradient Descent
text: For gradient descent to converge to a global minimum, certain conditions must be met. Consider the nature of the function being optimized and the learning rate used.

hintAnswer: A fixed learning rate can lead to convergence issues if not chosen appropriately.
title: Exploring Learning Rate
text: What effect does a fixed learning rate have on the convergence of gradient descent?
choices: A fixed learning rate can lead to convergence issues if not chosen appropriately.
It always leads to faster convergence
It has no effect on convergence
It may cause oscillations or divergence

hintAnswer: Gradient descent may converge to a local minimum depending on the function's landscape.
title: Global vs. Local Minimum
text: Does gradient descent always find the global minimum?
choices: Gradient descent may converge to a local minimum depending on the function's landscape.
No, it depends on the function
Only if the function is convex
Only with a variable learning rate
